Other high‑probability causes include intrinsic high‑degree AV block (degenerative conduction disease) with a junctional escape, AV‑nodal blocker (beta‑blocker or nondihydropyridine CCB) toxicity/overdose or medication effect, acute inferior myocardial infarction causing ischemic AV nodal dysfunction, and severe electrolyte disturbance (hyperkalemia) or other metabolic causes. 2. High‑degree AV block (third‑degree/complete heart block) from intrinsic conduction system disease — producing symptomatic bradycardia with junctional escape.
3. AV‑nodal blocker (beta‑blocker or nondihydropyridine calcium‑channel blocker) toxicity or excess (intentional overdose or accumulation) — causes severe bradycardia/AV block and altered mental status.
4. Acute inferior myocardial infarction with ischemic AV‑nodal dysfunction — can produce bradyarrhythmias and nausea/vomiting.
5. Severe electrolyte/metabolic disturbance (hyperkalemia, severe hypothyroidism, or uremia) — can produce profound bradycardia and junctional/escape rhythms.
